stages.name: Protectionism impacts
stages.title: Protectionism impacts
stages.sub: How quotas and subsidies affect consumers, domestic producers and foreign producers.

steps.q: A government tells importers they may bring in no more than 10,000 foreign cars this year, however many people want to buy. What kind of rule is this?
steps.right: A limit on the physical quantity allowed in
steps.wrong: An extra charge added to each car's price
steps.hint: Think about whether the rule caps the number of units, or adds to the price of each unit.

steps.q: A government pays domestic steel firms £50 for every tonne they produce, on top of what they earn from selling it. What has this done to their costs of producing each tonne?
steps.hint: The firm now receives extra money for each tonne made. Does that make producing cheaper or more expensive for them?

steps.q: Only 10,000 foreign cars are now allowed in, far fewer than before, and buyers can no longer easily choose the cheaper imported models. What happens to the prices and range of cars available to buyers?
steps.right: Prices rise and choice is reduced
steps.hint: With fewer imported cars on the market and fewer models to pick from, what happens to price and variety?

steps.q: Domestic steel firms now receive a subsidy that lowers their costs, while foreign steel still arrives at its normal price. Can domestic firms now compete more easily and sell more?
steps.right: Yes, they are shielded from competition and can raise output
steps.wrong: No, the subsidy makes no difference to their sales
steps.hint: Lower costs let domestic firms price more competitively against imports. What happens to their sales?

steps.q: Overseas car makers used to sell 50,000 cars into this market each year. Now only 10,000 imported cars are allowed in total. What happens to the overseas makers' sales and revenue from this market?
steps.right: They fall, since far fewer of their cars can be sold there
steps.wrong: They stay the same, since the cars are still just as good
steps.hint: The quota caps how many imported cars can enter, no matter how many foreign firms want to sell.
